meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'when?'.

examples.trans: When does the hardware shop open?
When did the bus arrive at the station?

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Often placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'spare' (مفتاح احتياط a spare key).

examples.trans: I have a spare key in the drawer.
We bought a spare valve for winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستعمل, بيستعمل).

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
I used the last valve in winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنكسر, بينكسر).

examples.trans: The brass pressure valve broke.
Not a single glass broke in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: باردة, plural: باردين).

examples.trans: Here, drink a glass of cold water.
My hands were cold from the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببيع, بيبيع).

examples.trans: The hardware shop sells this size.
I thought it was lost when we sold the house!

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تالتة, plural: تالتين).

examples.trans: The attic room is on the third floor.
He used to sit on the third step.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: The heating is working in all the rooms.
The heating pipe is warm now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تلوج.

examples.trans: The water is cold as ice.
Snow fell on the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جسور.

examples.trans: Cross the overpass toward downtown.
The old shop is past the overpass.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حجار.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Thank goodness everything is fine!
We arrived safely, thank goodness.

حِفِظ.gloss: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve

meanings.en: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحفظ, بيحفظ).

examples.trans: Old stone holds the warmth until morning.

examples.text: شكرا لأنك حفظت الشنتة طول الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Thank you for keeping the bag safe all week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخبار.

examples.trans: I have good news for you today!
They have no news yet.

meanings.note: Plural noun (from Persian khurda) used in دكان الخردوات ('hardware shop').

examples.trans: The hardware shop sells screws and wrenches.
I found the part at the hardware market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافية, plural: دافيين).

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth at night.
Morning warmth from the sun is comforting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دكاكين.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I bought milk and bread from the shop.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أدلة.

examples.trans: I bought the Amman travel guide.
The guesthouse is listed in the annual guide.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دوشات.

examples.trans: The shower water is hot and great.
The bathroom has a clean shower.

meanings.note: Used mainly in polite/earnest requests: أرجوك (to a man), أرجوكي (to a woman), أرجوكم (plural) — 'please!'.

examples.trans: Please write down that sentence!
Please do not open the white parcel.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Numeral 'seven' (عالسبعة 'at seven o'clock').

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I booked room seven yesterday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسبق, بيسبق).

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
You beat me to the kitchen by two minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سخانات.

examples.trans: We started the boiler before breakfast.
The boiler room is down in the basement.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سيئة, plural: سيئين).

examples.trans: I have bad news about the water heater.
The weather outside is not bad today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سياحية, plural: سياحيين).

examples.trans: We bought the Amman tourist guide.
The old quarter is a quiet tourist area.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, شتا means both the winter season and rain.

examples.trans: Winter water is very cold in the morning.
I love the sound of winter rain on the window.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صمامات.

examples.trans: We fitted a new brass valve on the boiler.
Make sure the valve is tightly shut.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صناديق.

examples.trans: The screwdriver is inside the toolbox.
We moved four boxes out of the hallway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضبط, بيضبط).

examples.trans: Set the alarm for six, Tariq.
The plan worked out one hundred percent!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضغوط.

examples.trans: The pressure valve on the boiler works.
Calm tea eases blood pressure.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Describes kind-hearted people (ناس طيبين) and pleasant smells/tastes (ريحة طيبة); standalone طيب means 'alright / well then'.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
The coffee smells wonderful in the morning!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عدد.

examples.trans: The screwdriver and wrench are in the toolbox.
He brought the tools to fix the boiler.

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.
We prepared a warm breakfast for the guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فقاعات.

examples.trans: There was an air bubble in the pipe.
Tiny bubbles rose in the boiling water.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مفتشين.

examples.trans: We thought he was a hotel inspector from the guidebook!
The inspector checked the building's safety features.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مقاسات.

examples.trans: This size fits you perfectly.
The shop sells all pipe sizes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: منبهات.

examples.trans: Set the alarm for six in the morning.
The alarm rang and we woke up early.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نايمة, plural: نايمين).

examples.trans: The new guest is sleeping on the third floor.
The whole neighbourhood is asleep and quiet.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, نحاس covers both yellow brass and red copper, often placed directly after a noun (مفاتيح نحاس brass keys).

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of نصف ('half'); used for half hours (السبعة ونص seven thirty) and quantities (نص كاسة half a glass).

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of وراء ('behind, past').

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: With two pronunciations in context: walla ('or' in choice questions: عالشارع ولا عالساحة؟) and wala ('not even / nor': ولا خدش 'not a single scratch', ولا يهمك 'do not worry at all').

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.
